newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Graningeverken to import Finnish power.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Graningeverken to import Finnish power.

text.p: Swedish power producer Graningeverken on Tuesday said it was to import up to 175 GWh of electricity from Finnish power company Pohjolan Voima Oy (PVO) over the rest of 1996.
The company said that from September 1 it was possible for Swedish power companies for the first time to take advantage of connections between Sweden and Finland.
This was previously limited to state power companies Vattenfall and Imatran Voima.
"Graninge has now reached an agreement related to importing Finnish power into Sweden for the rest of the year," the company said in a statement.
It said PVO is a power company that is owned jointly by a number of companies.
"The Finnish power will help to relieve the dry conditions that prevail in Sweden and Norway," Graninge's managing director Gunnar Larsson said in the statement,
